summary.text: Adrian Smith is the Republican incumbent seeking an eleventh term representing Nebraska's 3rd District. A Gering native, he worked as an educator and real estate agent, served on the Gering City Council and in the Nebraska Legislature, and was elected to the U.S. House in 2006. He sits on the Ways and Means Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Trade.

paragraphs.text: Born in Scottsbluff, Nebraska; his House website describes him as a Gering native whose family has lived in Nebraska for six generations.
Attended Liberty University from 1989 to 1990 before earning a B.A. from the University of Nebraska in 1993.
According to his House website, he worked as an educator and a real estate agent before his election to Congress.
Served on the Gering City Council from 1994 to 1998.
Served in the Nebraska State Senate from 1999 to 2007, representing District 48.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2006 and has served since 2007, representing Nebraska's 3rd District.

His House website says he has served on the Ways and Means Committee since 2010. In the 2025-2026 term he serves on Ways and Means (chair of the Trade Subcommittee and a member of the Health Subcommittee) and the Joint Committee on Taxation.

His House website cites his work on trade agreements, including the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, and on the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, and lists membership in the Agriculture Trade, Biofuels, Modern Agriculture and Rural caucuses and the House Democracy Partnership.
According to his House website, he and his wife, Andrea, live in Gering with their two children.
